planPadrino.heroSubtitle: Become a constant support for a young person transitioning to independent living.
planPadrino.queEsDesc: The Sponsorship Plan is a monthly sponsorship initiative where your economic contribution goes directly to covering the basic needs of a young person in the process of leaving the state protection system. As a sponsor, you become a fundamental pillar in a young person's journey toward autonomy, providing them with stability and hope.
planPadrino.beneficio1Desc: Your monthly contribution goes directly to a specific young person, allowing you to see the real impact of your support.
planPadrino.beneficio2Desc: You receive periodic updates on the progress and achievements of the young person you sponsor.
planPadrino.beneficio3Desc: You can establish a mentorship and emotional support relationship with the young person, guiding them in their transition.
planPadrino.beneficio4Desc: You receive a sponsorship certificate and recognition as part of the ASCEP sponsor network.

planPadrino.paso2Desc: We agree on a monthly contribution that fits your possibilities. You can donate through Vaki or bank transfer.
planPadrino.paso3Desc: Each month you will receive a report on the young person's progress, achievements, and challenges.
planPadrino.paso4Desc: Your constant support provides the young person with the stability needed to build their life project with confidence.
planPadrino.ctaDesc: Write to us and we will tell you all the details to start this beautiful work.

voluntariado.heroSubtitle: Your time and talent can transform a young person's life.
voluntariado.porqueDesc: Volunteering at ASCEP is an opportunity to share your knowledge, experiences, and time with young people who are building their life project outside the protection system. As a volunteer, you not only transform others' lives but also grow personally and professionally.

voluntariado.rol2Desc: Teach workshops in areas such as technology, art, sports, finance, communication, or any topic you master.

voluntariado.requisito4: Willingness to work with youth in vulnerable situations.
voluntariado.requisito5: Attend ASCEP's initial induction and training.
voluntariado.ctaDesc: Write to us and we will tell you how you can start being part of our volunteer team.

leyEgreso.title: State's Children Law
leyEgreso.subtitle: Law 2479 of 2025 - A step toward autonomy for youth in protection
leyEgreso.queEs: What is the State's Children Law
leyEgreso.queEsDesc: Law 2479 of 2025, known as the "State's Children Law", was approved by the Colombian Congress on July 15, 2025 and creates the National Comprehensive Support Program for graduates of the ICBF protection system. This law aims to guarantee comprehensive support, social inclusion and real opportunities for young people leaving the ICBF who lack family or community support networks. It was driven by ASCEP since 2019, initially championed by congressman Jhon Arley Murillo and taken up in 2023 by Senator Lorena Rios.
leyEgreso.obj1: Strengthen state services for young graduates
leyEgreso.obj2: Establish support networks with social and community organizations
leyEgreso.obj3: Facilitate social inclusion and access to job and educational opportunities
leyEgreso.obj4: Develop social, emotional, educational and job skills
leyEgreso.obj5: Provide economic support during the transition
leyEgreso.est1Desc: Creation of Support Units with interdisciplinary teams. Personalized support in life project, health, employment and autonomy.
leyEgreso.est2Desc: Monthly subsidy for 6 months after graduation, through the DPS.
leyEgreso.est3Desc: Basic, secondary and higher education (ICETEX, SENA). Formal employment and entrepreneurship with incentives. Loans and subsidies with preferential rates.
leyEgreso.est4Desc: Participation of CSOs, private sector, religious organizations and volunteers.
leyEgreso.est5Desc: Commitment signing and possibility of monitoring the program.
leyEgreso.dir1: Young people between 18 and 28 who lived under ICBF protection measures
leyEgreso.dir2: Youth about to graduate without family networks or support
leyEgreso.dir3: People with disabilities under ICBF protection who need permanent support
leyEgreso.dirExtra1Desc: Teams responsible for care and preparation for autonomous life of adolescents under protection.
leyEgreso.dirExtra2Desc: Entities interested in youth employability, education, mental health, housing, entrepreneurship, spirituality, culture and support networks.
leyEgreso.cambioDesc: The law creates the National Comprehensive Support Program, providing health, education, subsidies and psychosocial support. It includes Comprehensive Support Units to strengthen skills and economic support equivalent to 80% of the minimum wage for six months after leaving the system. It also promotes autonomy and comprehensive well-being through employment programs, business training and preferential credit lines.
leyEgreso.implementacionDesc: Law 2479 of 2025 assigns the Colombian Institute of Family Welfare (ICBF) a central and operational role in implementing its objectives. The ICBF, as head of the National Family Welfare System, has several key responsibilities:
leyEgreso.impl1: Formulate, coordinate and implement the National Comprehensive Support Program within 24 months of the law taking effect.
leyEgreso.impl2: Create and strengthen Graduate Support Units, made up of interdisciplinary teams.
leyEgreso.impl3: Incorporate the national registry of graduates.
leyEgreso.papelEgresadosDesc: Graduates of the protection system should not only be beneficiaries of Law 2479, but active subjects, co-responsible and protagonists of its implementation, monitoring and improvement. The law exists because organized graduates raised their voices; therefore, their natural role is to guard its meaning, monitor compliance and bring it to life in the territories.
leyEgreso.pe4: Social leaders and agents of change
leyEgreso.papelASCEPDesc: ASCEP is the organization called to sustain the meaning, implementation and social sustainability of Law 2479. It was not only its promoter: today it is its main social reference actor.
leyEgreso.pa1: Promoter and guardian of the spirit of the law
leyEgreso.pa3: Social and political oversight of implementation
leyEgreso.pa5: Generator of knowledge and good practices
leyEgreso.procesoDesc: The bill was driven by graduates themselves through ASCEP, backed by Senator Lorena Rios and with reports by Alexandra Vasquez and Jairo Cristo. It was approved in the Congress of the Republic and signed by President Gustavo Petro.
leyEgreso.participaDesc: Effective implementation requires commitment from everyone: government, civil society, private sector and media. You can raise awareness in your community, volunteer as a mentor, establish partnerships with ASCEP and ICBF, and advocate for public policies that guarantee the well-being of young graduates.
leyEgreso.ctaDesc: Join us to build a dignified future for every young graduate of the protection system.

home.heroTitle: Transforming how the State approaches the care and protection of children and youth
home.heroSubtitle: We are graduates of the state protection system, united to build a future with autonomy and dignity for every young person.
home.aboutDesc: We are a group of graduates from the Colombian State Protection System, united to improve the protection and restoration of rights for children, adolescents, and youth in the country. We appreciate the support received from the State, but recognize the need to evaluate and improve certain aspects of this system.
home.aboutItem1: We build capacities and skills in pre-graduates of the protection system
home.aboutItem2: We work with political actors to design projects that guarantee real conditions
home.aboutItem3: We facilitate the transition to adult life with confidence and autonomy
home.statsDesc: Each number represents a transformed life and a step toward a fairer and more effective protection system for Colombian youth.
home.testimonial1Text: ASCEP gave me the tools I needed to build my life project. Today I am an independent professional, grateful to everyone who believed in me.
home.testimonial2Text: Being part of ASCEP made me understand that I was not alone. The support network I found here was fundamental for my transition to adult life.
home.testimonial3Text: As a volunteer, I have seen firsthand the transformative impact of ASCEP's programs. Every young person who achieves autonomy is a victory for all of society.
home.ctaDesc: Your support, whether as a donor, volunteer, or ally, strengthens the support fabric that makes it possible for every young person to build their life project with dignity.
home.ctaFormMsg: Tell us how you would like to participate
home.retosDesc1: Adolescents and young people in the process of leaving the state protection system face significant challenges, such as defining their legal situation, rights violations, or the impact of forced displacement. These young people require comprehensive support to build their life project, access educational and employment opportunities, and achieve full social integration.
home.retosDesc2: We build capacities and skills in pre-graduates and graduates of the protection system.

modelo.title: Our Model
modelo.desc: Our model focuses on strengthening the self, as a foundation for young people leaving the protection system to manage their life project.
modelo.desc2: We work transversally across Carol Ryff's six dimensions of psychological well-being in all our processes.
modelo.dim1Desc: Positive valuation of oneself and one's own history.
modelo.dim2Desc: Ability to establish quality social relationships based on trust.
modelo.dim3Desc: Perception of control over one's environment and ability to create favorable surroundings.
modelo.dim4Desc: Ability to sustain one's own individuality and self-determination.
modelo.dim5Desc: Ability to have clear goals and define vital objectives.
modelo.dim6Desc: Development of individual potential to grow as a person.

quienesSomos.heroSubtitle: We are a group of graduates of the Colombian State Protection System who, based on our own experience, have come together to contribute to the transformation and improvement of how the State approaches the care and protection of children, adolescents, and young people in the country.
quienesSomos.historiaP1: We are a group of people who graduated from the Colombian State Protection System who, based on our own experience, have come together to contribute to the transformation and improvement of how the State, through its operators, addresses the care, protection and restoration of rights of children, adolescents and young people in the country.
quienesSomos.historiaP2: We recognize the support received from the State, but we also see the need to evaluate and improve certain aspects of the protection system to better serve young people transitioning to independence.
quienesSomos.historiaP3: Leaving the protection system is not a solitary journey. We have built a community where graduates support each other, share experiences, and grow together.
quienesSomos.historiaP4: Since 2019, we have been working tirelessly to transform how the State approaches the care and protection of children, adolescents, and young people in Colombia.
quienesSomos.historiaP5: Today, ASCEP is recognized nationally as a leading voice in the transformation of the protection system, advocating for the rights and well-being of young graduates.
quienesSomos.misionDesc: To accompany and strengthen young graduates of the Colombian State Protection System in their transition to autonomous adult life, through training programs, psychosocial support, and advocacy for public policies that guarantee their rights and well-being.
quienesSomos.visionDesc: A Colombia where every young person leaving the protection system has the tools, support networks, and opportunities needed to build their life project with autonomy and dignity.
quienesSomos.propositoCardDesc: To be the driving force behind a protection system that truly serves the comprehensive development of children, adolescents, and young people, ensuring they have real opportunities for a dignified life.
quienesSomos.equipoDesc: We are a team of graduates of the protection system, professionals, volunteers, and allies united by the conviction that every young person deserves a fair chance at life.
quienesSomos.enfoqueDesc: Our methodological approach combines psychosocial support, training in life skills, political advocacy, and community building to address the comprehensive needs of young graduates.
quienesSomos.ctaDesc: If you share our vision, we invite you to join as an ally, volunteer or donor.
